points.headline: Anthropic accuses Chinese labs of industrial-scale model copying.
points.body: Anthropic's September threat report details distillation campaigns by Alibaba, Moonshot AI and DeepSeek that escalated as competition tightened, alongside criminal misuse ranging from drone-swarm planning to bioweapons research. Six Chinese firms now stand accused, and Washington is urging US labs to identify Chinese users and quietly route them to weaker models.

points.headline: AI is collapsing the gap between bug and exploit.
points.body: Four separate groups were caught using the same Blue Moon exploit kit for Chrome and Windows, which researchers tie to a patch gap and faster AI-driven vulnerability discovery. Calif says AI helped it find a WeChat bug and write a zero-click remote exploit in about two days, and Wired showed an open-source model, stripped of its guardrails, breaking into household gadgets.

points.headline: OpenAI turns Astra into a platform, then runs short of compute.
points.body: The new Agents API offers managed cloud agents on the Codex harness with long-running sessions and tool use, and GPT-Live-1 brings full-duplex voice conversations to developers. Demand for GPT-6 Astra is heavy enough that OpenAI has paused new Pro subscriptions while it adds capacity.

points.headline: AI safety fears move from forums to parliaments.
points.body: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quit warning it is "crunch time for humanity", and UK lawmakers are raising alarms after a summer of rogue-agent incidents. OpenAI is asking whether antitrust law would even allow labs to coordinate a slowdown, and has added alignment researcher Paul Christiano to its Foundation board.

points.headline: Agents are moving into everyday work software.
points.body: Slack's new Surfaces builds dashboards, polls and reports from chat context, ChatGPT gained a Data agent and a Financial Services edition, and Amazon Quick's assistant is now generally available on desktop. Incumbents are hedging: Oracle argues AI will save it from the "SaaSpocalypse" rather than cause it.

points.headline: AI infrastructure keeps scaling, and the grid is the constraint.
points.body: Jensen Huang forecasts 70% Nvidia growth next year and insists its deals are not circular, while Samsung will help secure OpenAI's chip and memory supply. Google signed a 22-year nuclear power deal for a €13B Finland expansion, and a July fault in Ashburn knocked 3 GW of data-center load off the grid in seconds.
